title: A pseudo-coherent complex over a finite free algebra has a bounded above complex of finite free modules

standard_prerequisites.name: The cohomology of the complex is a finite module over the base ring in the degrees where it is nonzero, because the complex is pseudo-coherent over that ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite module whose surjection from a finite free module starts the construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: In a distinguished triangle, if two terms are pseudo-coherent then so is the third, which lets the cone of the comparison map be used in the induction
standard_prerequisites.use: Keeps the cone pseudo-coherent over the base ring so that the induction hypothesis applies to it.

core_obligations: Represent the object by a complex and use pseudo-coherence over the base ring to see that the cohomology vanishes in large degrees; let m be the smallest index with nonvanishing cohomology, whose cohomology is a finite module over the base (proof lines 8694-8699).
Choose a finite free module in degree m and a map to the complex there, killed by the differential and surjective on the m-th cohomology, drawn as the displayed diagram (proof lines 8699-8706).

Set up the descending induction on n at most m, the assertion being the existence of finite free modules in degrees at least n, differentials between them, and compatible maps to the complex such that the induced maps on cohomology are isomorphisms above n and surjective at n, with the modules vanishing above m (proof lines 8707-8715).
Base case: the construction of the previous paragraph is exactly the assertion for n equal to m (proof lines 8716-8719).

Induction step: form the cone of the comparison map; its cohomology vanishes in degrees at least n, it is pseudo-coherent over the base ring, and its n-th cohomology is a finite module, so a finite free module and a map from it onto that cohomology can be chosen (proof lines 8720-8750).

Use the map from the cone to build a finite free module in degree n minus one fitting into the diagram, extend the differential and the comparison map, and verify the two asserted properties, which completes the induction and hence the proof (proof lines 8751-8770).
proof_roadmap: Find the lowest nonvanishing cohomology and build the first finite free module (proof lines 8694-8706).
Set up the descending induction and dispose of its base case (proof lines 8707-8719).
Induction step: cone, finiteness of its cohomology, and the new finite free module (proof lines 8720-8770).
